get.description: Reads the database's own statistics on demand, as tempobase_monitor (a member of pg_monitor that runs only tempoBase's fixed queries): connections against the limit, cache hit ratio and size (overview); the top statements from pg_stat_statements (queries); sessions with what blocks them (sessions); table and index sizes and use (tables, indexes); and hints about what needs a look. Nothing is stored. Overview, tables and indexes need level schema; queries and sessions read, with statement values redacted for callers who see sensitive columns masked. Views the caller may not see, or the server can't give, are listed in `unavailable`.

Cancels the session's running query, or with `terminate` ends the session (its connection and open transaction), as the owner. `query_started_at` (the session's `query_at`) makes sure only that query is cancelled, never a later one; a session that ended or moved on is 409. Level write, which tokens never have on production; ending a session on production needs `confirm` set to the connection's name. Audited as data.cancel or data.terminate.

post.description:
Runs one statement as tempobase_reader in a READ ONLY transaction; several statements in one string are refused. Results are capped by `limit` (default 10 000, at most 100 000) and 64 MB, cells over 8 KB are truncated. Level read; masked callers' SQL runs as tempobase_reader_masked, which can't select sensitive columns.

The response is NDJSON (`application/x-ndjson`): one DataQueryFrame per line. A `header` frame (columns), `rows` frames of up to 500 rows, then exactly one `end` frame (row count, truncated, duration) or `error` frame (what the database reported, possibly after rows). Permission and validation errors are normal problem responses before any frame. Closing the connection cancels the query.

200.description: NDJSON stream of DataQueryFrame, one per line
